events.title: Workers’ Compensation Appeal Tribunal: WCAT replaced the Workers’ Compensation Review Board and the Appeal Division of the Workers’ Compensation Board.

evidence.source_title: WCAT: A Short History of the Workers’ Compensation Appeal System

events.title: British Columbia Farm Industry Review Board: Specified provisions took effect and regulatory Farm Practices Board / BC Marketing Board wording changed to BC Farm Industry Review Board.
events.interpretation_notes: This verifies the regulatory transition, not every element of a fully reconstructed legal amalgamation.

events.title: BC Financial Services Authority: BCFSA commenced operations and assumed FICOM regulatory accountabilities. This is operational commencement, not necessarily the legal incorporation date.
Financial Institutions Commission: The official history associates FICOM dissolution with full implementation of BCFSA in November 2019.
events.interpretation_notes: Do not borrow the separate operational-start day as an independently verified dissolution day.

events.title: BCFSA and real estate regulators: BCFSA integrated RECBC and Office of the Superintendent of Real Estate regulatory accountabilities.
events.interpretation_notes: The continuing statutory Superintendent role is not labelled abolished.

events.title: BC Energy Regulator: BC Oil and Gas Commission became BC Energy Regulator effective 17 February; the notice was issued on 22 February. Expanded-mandate provisions were staged.

evidence.source_title: BCER: Transitioning to BC Energy Regulator (IU 2023-04)

events.title: SkilledTradesBC: Industry Training Authority became SkilledTradesBC. This body is distinct from the similarly named appeal board.
Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board: Industry Training Appeal Board was renamed when the Skilled Trades BC Act came into force.

evidence.source_title: Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board 2023/24 Annual Report

events.title: Energy Resource Appeal Tribunal: Oil and Gas Appeal Tribunal was renamed Energy Resource Appeal Tribunal, on a different date from the regulator rename.

evidence.source_title: Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board 2023/24 Annual Report

events.title: BC Timber Sales: BCTS replaced the Small Business Forest Enterprise Program within the Ministry of Forests.

evidence.source_title: Forest Practices Board: BCTS 100 Mile House audit

events.interpretation_notes: The older special-account creation date is not the BCTS program founding date.

events.title: Tourism British Columbia: Repeal dissolved Tourism BC and vested assets and obligations in government. The commencement table fixes 1 April 2010.

evidence.source_title: Budget Measures Implementation Act (No. 2), 2009, SBC c. 14

events.interpretation_notes: Destination BC is a later corporation, not automatically one uninterrupted identity.

events.title: Destination BC Corp.: Destination BC was established under the Business Corporations Act; operational commencement is separate.
Destination BC Corp.: Destination BC began operations after its November 2012 establishment.
Royal British Columbia Museum Corporation: The corporation was formed under the Museum Act on 1 April 2003.

evidence.source_title: Royal BC Museum 2023/24 Statement of Financial Information

events.interpretation_notes: Do not replace the older museum or Archives histories with a 2003 founding date.

events.title: Community Living British Columbia: CLBC was established and assumed adult community living service responsibility. Staff support for children’s services under agreement was distinct from retained MCFD funding, policy, monitoring and accountability.

evidence.source_title: CLBC financial statements for nine months ended 31 March 2006

events.interpretation_notes: Not a transfer of every children’s-service responsibility.

events.title: Provincial Capital Commission: OIC 128/2014 brought the Act into force on 25 March 2014. The Act dissolved the commission and vested its property and obligations in government.

evidence.locator: Clause (a), together with Dissolution Act s. 2

events.interpretation_notes: 24 March assent is not the commencement date.

events.title: BC Human Rights Commission: The report dates elimination of the Commission and Advisory Council to proclamation on 31 March 2003; the existing Tribunal continued under direct access.

evidence.source_title: BC Human Rights Tribunal 2003/04 Annual Report

events.interpretation_notes: No automatic continuity with a later commissioner’s office.

events.title: BC Human Rights Tribunal: The pre-existing Tribunal moved to direct complaint access and received transferred files.

evidence.source_title: BC Human Rights Tribunal 2003/04 Annual Report

events.interpretation_notes: A process change, not the Tribunal’s original establishment.
